title: Traffic Garden — latency & cost poster Q3 2029 (sketch)
content:
One-page poster sketch intended for console placement and sales collateral. Lightweight, visually oriented language but here represented as plain text. Goal: show tradeoffs across strategies for dealing with short, high-frequency spikes (microbursts) and sustained traffic increases. Keep it actionable: what to toggle in Console and expected payoffs.

Top-line message
- You can shave p95/p99 by 2x–4x with small operational levers while keeping $/k queries within 1.2x of baseline. Big wins come from combining targeted prewarm slots + short-lived KV cache + adaptive batching. Quantization reduces cost but can increase tail latency if misapplied during bursts.

Quick legend (for charts below)
- Baseline: no prewarm, static batch=1, model: base-16 FP.
- Small-batch: fixed batch size 4.
- Dyn-batch: adaptive batching tuned to max latency budget 250 ms.
- Prewarm: reserved short-lived workers spun when signals detect burst start.
- KV-cache: prefix cache hit rate applied to repeated prefixes in session.
- Quant4: 4-bit quantized runtime (best-effort accuracy-preserving profile).
- Hybrid-fallback: primary model with automatic fallback to smaller variant for p99-heavy requests.

ASCII mini-table: scenario snapshots (sample workload: chat-style 60–120 token responses)
Scenario                       | Avg(ms) | P95(ms) | P99(ms) | $/1k req
-------------------------------|---------|---------|---------|---------
Baseline                       | 120     | 340     | 900     | 18.5
Small-batch (4)                | 98      | 260     | 720     | 14.2
Dyn-batch (adaptive)           | 85      | 220     | 480     | 11.0
Prewarm (short slots) + KV     | 60      | 150     | 260     | 12.5
Quant4 (aggressive)            | 90      | 240     | 600     | 8.3
Hybrid-fallback (small model)  | 70      | 200     | 420     | 9.7
Prewarm + Dyn-batch + KV (combo)| 55     | 140     | 240     | 10.8

Notes on numbers (quick caveats)
- Numbers are representative single-cluster runs on r4-class GPUs; absolute ms and $/k will vary by model size and region. Use relative deltas for decision-making.
- $/1k req is estimated infra + amortized model cost; it assumes 50% cache-hit effectiveness for KV-enabled scenarios and conservative utilization.
- Prewarm cost includes short reserved slots charged during detected burst windows — the economics improve when bursts are predictable (seasonal events).

Simple ascii-sparklines (p99 over time for three strategies, x-axis = 0–60s burst window)
Baseline p99:   |▁▂▃▅▇███████████
Small-batch p99:|▁▁▂▂▃▅████─────
Combo p99:      |▁▁▁▁▂▂▂▃▃───▁───

Interpretation: baseline ramps to long tails quickly. Small fixed batching reduces average/median but still suffers on extreme p99. Combination of prewarm + dyn-batch + cache keeps p99 compressed even as concurrency spikes.

Operational knobs to expose in Console (recommended default settings and tooltips)
- Burst sensitivity: integer [0..100] (default 40). Tooltip: "How aggressively we prewarm. Higher -> faster reaction, higher reserved cost."
- Prewarm slot TTL: seconds (default 30s). Tooltip: "How long prewarm slots remain idle before reclamation. Shorter -> lower cost, more cold-starts."
- Dynamic batch max latency: ms (default 250 ms). Tooltip: "Target P90 budget used to form batches; smaller budgets mean less batching and higher infra cost."
- KV cache window: tokens (default 512). Tooltip: "Prefix length where cache applies; helps repeated prompts and assistant beginnings."
- Quant profile: {safety threshold}% (default 95). Tooltip: "Only apply quant to requests where eval pass rate >= threshold."

Tradeoff cheat sheet (one-line takeaways)
- Need lowest p99 at any cost: prewarm aggressively + accept 1.2–1.5x $/k.
- Need best $/k with reasonable tails: quant + hybrid-fallback yields ~0.45x cost vs baseline but keep hybrid fallbacks to bound p99.
- Spike-proof, low operational overhead: dyn-batching + light prewarm + KV cache (combo) — sweet spot for PLG customers.

Short decision flow (for SREs / Solutions Eng)
- Are bursts predictable (calendar/campaign)? -> Use prewarm slots scheduled at event windows + KV cache prefill.
- Are bursts user-driven and unpredictable? -> Enable dyn-batch + micro-prewarm (low TTL) + fallback smaller model.
- Is cost the dominant constraint? -> Evaluate quantized runtime with A/B on held-out prompts; monitor quality/regressions.

Quality guardrails (must-haves in Console before enabling aggressive cost knobs)
- Prompt-specific eval sets (per-customer) with automatic regression alert on ROUGE/EM/semantic-sim thresholds.
- Canary funnel: 1% traffic -> 5% -> 25% -> 100% with automated rollback on p99 or token-error spikes.
- Instrumentation: per-route p50/p95/p99, cost per route, cache-hit histograms, batch-size distribution.

Example micro-play (30-minute runbook for a sudden flash sale spike)
1) Increase burst sensitivity to 70 for 10 min (Console quick-action). Expected immediate p99 reduction ~30%.
2) Increase prewarm slots to +15% capacity (short TTL). Monitor $/1k; revert after 20–30m.
3) Enable KV cache prefill for top-10 repeated prompts (manual list). Expect 10–25% fewer tokens generated for affected sessions.
4) If p99 still > threshold, flip hybrid-fallback for non-critical endpoints (route tag). This reduces p99 at the cost of some quality degradation for a tiny fraction of queries.

Suggested poster CTA (what we want Console users to do)
- "Try the Spike Button" — ephemeral run that deploys prewarm+cache+dyn-batch for 15 minutes to see impact. Show the delta panel (p50/p95/p99 and $/k) before/after.

Outstanding questions / open work (for follow-up experiments)
- Quantization interplay with batching: does aggressive batching amplify quant noise on edge tokens? (ENG-3271 experiment)
- Telemetry: can we expose batch-size vs tail-latency heatmap per route without exploding cardinality?
- Model routing fallback heuristics: TTL and warm-up cost of tiny models vs model switch latency.

Appendix: quick links to artifacts and experiments
- ENG-3271 (burst sensitivity prototype)
- experimental run artifacts: s3://redwood-bench/traffic-garden/q3-2029 (note: placeholder)
- Confluence page: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/traffic-garden

Author notes (for internal reviewers)
- This is a poster sketch intended to be translated into a console panel + 1-sheet for sales. Keep the ascii charts as input to the designer. We deliberately keep numbers illustrative; each customer page should show live deltas calculated from their telemetry.

End of sketch.
